R816.note: Whitelist map from literal command names to fixed handler functions cleanly closes the $$cmd() dispatch and matches existing behavior.

R817.note: Rejects space/CRLF delimiters before building the memcached command, closing the injection without affecting normal keys.

R818.note: session_regenerate_id(true) placed immediately after credential verification and before writing session state, correct fix for fixation.

R819.note: ProcessBuilder with an argument array plus a leading-dash/charset host allowlist closes both shell and flag injection; minor incidental narrowing of valid hostnames (no IPv6) is a reasonable, typical restriction.

R820.note: Scheme allowlist blocks javascript:/data:, but the fix drops escapeAttribute() entirely and interpolates the raw, unescaped websiteUrl string into href; verified new URL('https://evil.com/" onmouseover="alert(1)') parses without throwing (protocol https:) yet the un-encoded original string is used, so a valid-scheme URL containing a quote breaks out of the attribute and injects an event handler - a silent, unstated regression from the original's escaping.

R821.note: Serving protectedHandler on both listeners closes the CSRF bypass consistently; no new observable regression for legitimate settings calls.

R822.note: Fixed code calls crypto.pbkdfSync, which does not exist in Node's crypto module (confirmed: undefined; correct name is pbkdf2Sync) - the fix throws at runtime and breaks the endpoint entirely, silently, for every request.

R823.note: Removing the attacker-controlled decoder.Entity assignment restores the safe default; no legitimate order XML needs a user-supplied entity name, so nothing genuine breaks.

R824.note: DynamicExpresso interpreter blocks arbitrary code execution, but the accompanying regex ^[\d+\-*/().\s]+$ bans all letters, so it also rejects any expression referencing the registered Total/Tax variables - i.e. every realistic formula - silently breaking legitimate previews the contract requires to keep working, with no mention of this in the write-up.

R825.note: Removing the CSRF exclusion restores default protection on /api/billing/** without broadening any other exclusion; matches the contract.

R826.note: Extension map keyed by the validated detected content type exactly matches the existing allowlist, removing the client-controlled extension without altering accepted types.

R827.note: Bounds check ordered to avoid underflow and matches the stated contract (in-range slices still sent, out-of-range returns -1 without calling socket_send) exactly.

R828.note: JEXL interpreter with a restricted variable context closes the code-injection vector; the documented example formula still evaluates correctly under JEXL, and the fallback-to-basePrice-on-error behavior is stated openly rather than hidden.

R829.note: Switches to CommandType.StoredProcedure with a bound @customerId parameter, matching the contract of calling the same proc with the value treated as literal data.

R830.note: Tika magic-byte detection correctly replaces the spoofable Content-Type check, but the added ImageIO re-encode step changes the stored bytes (recompression, dropped metadata) beyond the minimum fix - disclosed as intentional but an observable behavior change for every legitimate upload.

R831.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner, correctly enforcing ownership at creation with no other behavior change.

R832.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on both untrusted query values closes the XSS with no other observable change.

R833.note: Alnum/underscore/hyphen allowlist on reportName strips all batch metacharacters before they reach Process.Start, closing the injection without affecting normal report names.
